introduction: On this most holy night, the Church keeps vigil for the Lord's Resurrection. We begin in darkness, with the new fire and the Easter candle, the sign of Christ our light. We listen to the great story of salvation, from creation to the crossing of the sea and the promises of the prophets. Tonight catechumens are baptized and confirmed and receive the Eucharist for the first time, and we all renew our baptismal promises. Christ is risen!

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, on this night of light we rejoice with the newly baptized. Let us pray to the Father, who raised his Son from the dead.
intentions: For the Church throughout the world, keeping vigil tonight: that the light of the risen Christ may shine through her in every land. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the newly baptized and all who have been received into full communion: that they may walk in newness of life and persevere in faith. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who live in darkness, fear or despair: that the Easter light may reach them and give them hope. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who have died, especially those we have loved: that they may share in the Resurrection of Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves, who have renewed our baptismal promises: that we may live as people who have died to sin and are alive to God. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God of life, on this night you raised your Son from the dead and gave new life to your children in Baptism. Keep us faithful to the promises we have made, and fill us with the joy of the Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: He has risen
reflection.body:
The Easter Vigil tells the whole story of our salvation in one night. It begins with creation: "God saw everything that he had made, and, behold, it was very good." It continues with Abraham, who told his son, "God will provide himself the lamb for a burnt offering, my son." Then comes the night when Israel crossed the sea and "the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left." Through the prophets God invites us: "Come, everyone who thirsts, to the waters!" and promises, "I will also give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit within you."

All these readings lead to the font. Paul explains what happens there: "We were buried therefore with him through baptism into death, that just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we also might walk in newness of life." Tonight the catechumens pass through those waters, as Israel passed through the sea, from slavery to freedom.

Mark's Gospel takes us to the tomb at dawn. Three women go to anoint the body, worried about a practical problem: "Who will roll away the stone from the door of the tomb for us?" When they arrive, the stone has already been rolled back. A young man in white tells them: "Don't be amazed. You seek Jesus, the Nazarene, who has been crucified. He has risen! He is not here."

Then he gives them a mission: "But go, tell his disciples and Peter." Peter, who had denied him three times, is named. The risen Lord has not given up on him.

We often come to God worried about the stones in our lives, the things we cannot move on our own. Tonight the Church tells us that the heaviest stone has already been rolled away. When you renew your baptismal promises and are sprinkled with the Easter water, say your yes with joy. Christ is risen, and he goes before us.
